notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2025, as the village reported them in its F-65 Annual Local Unit Fiscal Report to the Michigan Department of Treasury. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Shiawassee County and the township the village is part of.
Village residents also pay the township the village is part of, which is listed separately.

Spending is reported by function for the general fund, other governmental funds, enterprise funds (water, sewer and other utilities) and component units (such as downtown development authorities). Capital outlay has no function, so enterprise capital counts as utilities and the rest is spread over the other spending in proportion.
Internal service funds ($104,910 of their revenue and spending) are left out, since the departments they serve report that spending.
Borrowing, transfers between funds, sales of capital assets, depreciation and extraordinary items are left out.
General government, courts, community and economic development, and redevelopment and public housing count as overhead.
Debt is total long-term debt at year end, as reported on the F-65.
Political money is not scored: Michigan local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside Village of Morrice's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-18.

A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Michigan yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
